children: Although investors remain skeptical about the sustainability of artificial intelligence
have already partially priced in these concerns through sharp valuation de-ratings across AI infrastructure stocks, according to new research from Goldman Sachs.

The median AI infrastructure stock has de-rated from 32x consensus forward earnings in April to 22x today, Goldman wrote in a note to clients published earlier this week. When comparing recent changes in market cap to recent changes in earnings—a signal of how long markets expect current earnings strength to persist—expectations appear most elevated among optical networking, electrical grid and liquid cooling stocks, while outlooks remain most conservative among semiconductors
Semiconductor valuations embed particularly skeptical views about earnings durability. Memory stocks
trade at a 2-year forward price-to-earnings ratio of just 4x, half their 15-year average, despite enjoying gross margins of roughly 80%—more than double historical norms.

For memory stock P/Es to return to their 15-year average, earnings would need to decline by approximately 50%. Fabless chip stocks present a more compelling opportunity: their margins sit only modestly above historical averages, and earnings would need to decline just 10% to bring valuations back to normal levels, according to Goldman, which maintained Buy ratings on Nvidia
valuations have de-rated to their lowest levels in over a decade, now trading just four turns above the median S&P 500
company—the smallest premium on record, the note said. The combination of decelerating capex growth and improving free cash flow visibility should serve as positive catalysts for these stocks.

Goldman noted that U.S. hyperscalers are on track to spend $800B in capex this year, with consensus expecting $1.1T in 2027—investment levels as a share of GDP not seen since the railroad build-out of the late 1800s. Goldman estimates hyperscalers need some $300B in annual AI revenues to break even on their 2026-2027 capex investments.
While current estimated AI revenues remain below that threshold, cloud revenues have accelerated sharply, with combined backlogs from major providers exceeding $1.7T.

The application layer would need to generate roughly $1T in annual revenues for hyperscalers to earn solid returns—a figure comparable to the $1.5T in global software spending in 2026 and the $1.8T in potential U.S. labor productivity gains economists estimate will eventually accrue to capital.
